title: Implement SML’97 language core
description: Track the staged implementation of the Standard ML language in Nassau before expanding the Standard Basis Library. Use the Definition of Standard ML (Revised) as the language authority, preserve fixture-based oracle testing against SML/NJ and MLton, and exclude implementation-specific extensions unless explicitly chosen.
acceptance_criteria: Core SML’97 language constructs are implemented in staged, reviewable slices with fixture coverage; remaining gaps are explicit before Basis Library work begins.

title: Lex character literals and complete string escapes
description: Support character literals and SML string escape forms, including control and decimal escapes and whitespace continuation gaps, in addition to the currently recognized newline, tab, quote, and backslash escapes. Report malformed and unterminated forms at accurate spans.
close_reason: Implemented the lexical forms and added fixture-based end-to-end coverage; cargo fixture and REPL suites, cargo check, and formatting checks pass.

title: Add end-to-end fixtures for completed lexical forms
description: As parser support lands, add fixture coverage for each completed lexical form, including valid token usage and malformed literals/identifiers that should be rejected. Keep fixtures under tests/fixtures or tests/repl, compare with SML/NJ and MLton where their behavior is specified, and do not add Rust unit tests.
close_reason: Implemented the lexical forms and added fixture-based end-to-end coverage; cargo fixture and REPL suites, cargo check, and formatting checks pass.

title: Lex SML alphanumeric identifiers, type variables, and reserved words
description: Add the SML alphanumeric identifier forms, including apostrophes in identifiers, type variables beginning with one or more apostrophes, and the complete SML’97 reserved-word set. Preserve identifier spelling and distinguish lexical classes needed by parsing. Current coverage only accepts ASCII letter-starting words with alphanumeric/underscore tails and reserves val, div, if, then, else, true, and false.
close_reason: Implemented SML alphanumeric identifiers, apostrophe-bearing names, type-variable tokens, and the reserved-word set; cargo check passes.

title: Lex symbolic identifiers and reserved punctuation
description: Implement maximal-munch handling for SML symbolic identifiers, reserved symbolic tokens, punctuation, and qualification dots. Distinguish single reserved symbols such as # and | from valid longer symbolic identifiers, and preserve the operator spelling for later infix parsing. Current coverage hard-codes a few operators and rejects most SML punctuation.
close_reason: Implemented the lexical forms and added fixture-based end-to-end coverage; cargo fixture and REPL suites, cargo check, and formatting checks pass.

title: Lex all SML numeric and word constants
description: Support decimal and hexadecimal integers, decimal and hexadecimal word literals, decimal floating-point literals with exponent forms, and SML’s tilde sign handling. Validate malformed forms and avoid prematurely narrowing literal range in the lexer. Current coverage only accepts unsigned decimal digits and decimal fractions.
close_reason: Implemented the lexical forms and added fixture-based end-to-end coverage; cargo fixture and REPL suites, cargo check, and formatting checks pass.

title: Implement functors and advanced module features
description: Support functor declarations/applications and the remaining SML’97 module constructs, including higher-level sharing constraints, with focused typing and runtime fixtures.

title: Establish core SML’97 conformance inventory
description: Audit the Definition against Nassau’s parser, static semantics, and runtime; curate categorized fixture coverage and document unsupported constructs or intentional divergences before Basis expansion.

title: Implement references and imperative expressions
description: Add ref allocation/dereference/assignment and the SML sequencing/while behaviors needed by the language, with correct typing, evaluation order, and runtime representation.

title: Implement modules: signatures, structures, and opaque matching
description: Support signatures, structures, sharing/type specifications, transparent and opaque ascription, and signature matching according to SML’97. Add fixtures that check abstraction and type equality.

title: Implement Hindley–Milner type inference and polymorphism
description: Replace the current small type checker with SML type variables, unification, generalization/instantiation, value restriction, equality types, overloaded literals/operators, and useful type errors. Cover polymorphic functions and let-bound values with fixtures.

title: Implement datatypes, constructors, and type declarations
description: Add datatype declarations, constructor environments, type synonyms, replicated datatypes, and abstype as supported by SML’97. Test constructor scoping, recursion, and type identity.

title: Implement exceptions and exception handling
description: Add exception declarations/replication, raise, handle, and propagation semantics, including interaction with pattern matching and runtime values. Use oracle fixtures for normal and exceptional paths.

title: Implement SML patterns and pattern matching
description: Support wildcard, variable, constant, tuple/record, constructor, list, layered, and alternative patterns as specified. Add exhaustiveness/redundancy diagnostics where feasible and fixtures for matching semantics and failures.

title: Implement declarations and recursive bindings
description: Support val patterns, fun declarations, mutually recursive functions, local declarations, sequencing, and declaration scope rules. Preserve SML’s non-recursive val binding behavior and recursive function semantics.

title: Complete SML lexical syntax and literals
description: Coordinate implementation of Nassau’s missing SML’97 lexical forms through the child issues. Existing support includes nested comments, simple letter-starting identifiers, a small reserved-word subset, decimal integer/real literals, and basic string escapes. The focused issues define the remaining lexical gaps. Add end-to-end fixtures as parser support permits; do not add Rust unit tests.
acceptance_criteria: The child lexical feature issues are complete, all SML’97 lexical forms needed by the implemented language are represented without losing source spans, and fixture coverage exists wherever the parser can exercise those forms.
close_reason: Implemented the lexical forms and added fixture-based end-to-end coverage; cargo fixture and REPL suites, cargo check, and formatting checks pass.

title: Implement general expressions and precedence
description: Replace the integer-only expression grammar with SML expression parsing and specified precedence/associativity, including application, infix operators, selectors, sequences, let, case, if, and while. Keep parsing separate from type inference and execution.

title: Use SML/NJ as the sole fixture oracle
description: Remove slow MLton compilation from the fixture harness and use SML/NJ checks for regular and list fixtures.
close_reason: Fixture comparisons now use SML/NJ and no longer invoke MLton

title: Run list type fixtures as independent tests
description: The list type integration test currently loops over fixtures inside one test, so Cargo runs the group serially. Register each list fixture as an independent parallel test trial.
close_reason: List type fixtures now run through the recursive parallel fixture harness

title: Run each SML fixture in its own test
description: The fixture harness currently compares every SML fixture in one sequential integration test, preventing Cargo test parallelism. Register each fixture as an independent test while preserving the MLton oracle comparison behavior.
close_reason: Registered each SML fixture as an independent parallel test trial

title: Add FileCheck assertions for compiled and REPL fixtures
description: Replace exit-code-only fixture checks with stable FileCheck expectations for compiled program output and REPL output. Ensure compiled and REPL fixtures run with the original fixture directory as their working directory, and assert semantic failures return non-zero.

title: Add list runtime representation for Cranelift and JIT
description: Implement runtime storage and value handling for lists in compiled programs and the persistent REPL JIT. Choose a Cranelift-compatible representation for heap-allocated list values, support allocations and cross-chunk REPL values safely, and keep representation consistent with inferred element types. This ticket depends on list syntax/types/inference being established first. Add end-to-end executable and REPL tests plus SML/NJ or MLton oracle fixtures; include nested lists and values surviving across REPL chunks.
acceptance_criteria: List values compile and execute through the object/compiler path and JIT REPL; nested and empty lists are represented correctly; list values can be bound and carried across REPL chunks without invalid pointers or lifetime issues; e2e and oracle tests cover supported behavior.
close_reason: Implemented heap-backed list values for compiled programs and persistent JIT REPL chunks; valid and invalid fixture status coverage passes.

title: Add list syntax, types, and inference
description: Add SML-style list literal syntax and semantic typing to Nassau. Parse empty and non-empty list literals (including nested lists), add list types, and implement type inference/unification so element types are consistent and empty lists can be resolved from context. Define and document the chosen behavior for unconstrained empty lists and polymorphic list values. Add end-to-end compiler/REPL coverage and SML/NJ or MLton oracle fixtures, including valid lists and type-error cases where the oracle harness supports them.
acceptance_criteria: List literal syntax and list types are specified; inference handles homogeneous and nested lists plus empty-list constraints; mismatched element types and unresolved empty lists produce clear diagnostics; e2e and oracle tests cover the supported semantics.
notes: Implemented list literal tokenization/parsing and recursive list type inference, including homogeneous and nested lists and polymorphic reuse of empty lists. Fixture sweep under tests/fixtures/lists checks valid and invalid examples against Nassau, SML/NJ, and MLton. Executable list values are covered by the dependent Cranelift/JIT runtime ticket.
close_reason: Implemented list literal parsing, recursive list typing/inference, and fixture-based SML/NJ/MLton frontend coverage; list execution is covered by the dependent runtime ticket.

title: Add if then else expressions
description: Implement Standard ML conditional expressions across lexing, parsing, semantic analysis, Cranelift codegen, REPL evaluation, and SML/NJ parity fixtures.
close_reason: Added Boolean literals and typed if-then-else expressions through all execution paths

title: Document end-of-task commit policy
description: Update repository AGENTS.md to allow a one-line commit at task completion and prohibit pushes.
close_reason: Updated project instructions to permit one-line task-end commits and prohibit remote pushes

title: Add inclusive comparisons and inequality
description: Add >=, <=, and Standard ML inequality <> across lexer, parser, semantic analysis, code generation, REPL evaluation, and SML/NJ parity fixtures.
close_reason: Implemented >=, <=, and <> through lexer, parser, sema, codegen, and SML/NJ-backed REPL fixtures

title: Add relational comparison operators
description: Implement >, <, and = expressions across parsing, semantic analysis, code generation, REPL evaluation, and end-to-end parity coverage. Semantic analysis must require operand types to match.
close_reason: Added relational operators with sema validation, Cranelift lowering, and SML/NJ-backed REPL fixtures

title: Simplify parse expectation errors
description: Replace the many ParseErrorKind expectation variants with one Expect(String) variant whose display adds the expected prefix.
close_reason: Replaced granular parser expectation variants with Expect(String)

title: Move semantic source spans to frontends
description: Make semantic errors location-free enum variants, return the offending expression separately from analysis, and have main and the REPL build source diagnostics from the expression spans.
close_reason: SemanticError is now a location-free enum; main and REPL construct a separate source diagnostic using the offending expression span.

title: Wrap semantic error kinds with one span
description: Move source spans from individual semantic error variants to a single location-bearing SemanticError wrapper, preserving typed error kinds and enabling conversions from located parse expressions.
close_reason: SemanticError now wraps a SemanticErrorKind enum alongside one source span, with tuple From conversion for located errors.

title: Model semantic errors with variants
description: Replace the message-based semantic error structure with typed variants for unbound variables, arithmetic operand failures, type mismatches, and integer range errors.
close_reason: Semantic errors are now structured enum variants with preserved source spans.

title: Introduce semantic analysis phase
description: Add src/sema.rs to centralize type environments and operator typing, including the integer/real arithmetic rules, then run semantic analysis before backend compilation and REPL evaluation.
close_reason: Added a stateful Analyzer with scope operations, transactional environment updates, centralized type checking for arithmetic and built-ins, and invoked it before code generation and REPL execution.

title: Add real literals and floating point division
description: Implement real literals and typed arithmetic so / follows Standard ML real division semantics, while retaining integer div. Include an end-to-end REPL and compiled-code fixture compared with SML implementations.
close_reason: Added real literals and f64 arithmetic with real-only slash division, retained integer div, and covered REPL results plus the SML/MLton fixture.

title: Add subtraction multiplication and division
description: Extend integer expressions and Cranelift lowering with subtraction, multiplication, and signed integer division. Exercise precedence and all arithmetic operators through existing end-to-end compiler and REPL oracle harnesses.
close_reason: Added - * / with multiplicative precedence and matching signed Cranelift operations, plus oracle fixture coverage.

title: Compare Nassau REPL sessions with SML/NJ
description: Separate REPL integration tests from the compiled executable versus MLton fixture tests. Feed source to Nassau and an SML/NJ interpreter process, normalize prompts and declaration echoes, and compare observable output and process status. Allow configuring the local SML/NJ executable.
close_reason: Added a dedicated configurable SML/NJ REPL integration harness and removed REPL execution from the MLton compiled-executable test.

title: Add variables and integer addition
description: Extend the language from special-case effects to named val bindings and integer expressions with addition, and add end-to-end coverage that compares direct execution, the REPL harness, and MLton.
close_reason: Added named integer bindings and addition, persistent REPL bindings, and three-way end-to-end comparisons against MLton.

title: Allow bare effect expressions in the REPL
description: Enable REPL input such as print "hello" without requiring the file-mode val _ = declaration, while keeping file parsing unchanged.
close_reason: REPL-mode parsing now accepts bare print and POSIX exit expressions while file parsing remains declaration-only.

title: Make the REPL the default frontend
description: Start the JIT REPL when Nassau is invoked without a source file, while retaining file compilation when a path is provided.
close_reason: Nassau now starts the REPL with no source argument and compiles when given a file path.

title: Add a Cranelift JIT REPL frontend
description: Add an interactive frontend that parses and executes currently supported SML declaration chunks using Cranelift JIT while sharing parsing and lowering with native compilation.
close_reason: Added a shared Cranelift code-generation path with a JIT-backed REPL frontend for supported SML chunks.

title: Discover all SML test fixtures
description: Update the MLton oracle integration test to discover and compare every SML source fixture in tests/fixtures instead of naming a single fixture.
close_reason: The oracle test now discovers each .sml fixture under tests/fixtures and compares each against MLton.

title: Use POSIX exit signature and compare against MLton
description: Support Posix.Process.exit (Word8.fromInt n) in the SML subset and extend the integration harness to compare Nassau and MLton stdout and process status for the same fixture.
close_reason: Nassau now accepts the Basis-qualified POSIX exit form and integration tests compare stdout and status against MLton.

title: Add print and exit compiler builtins
description: Add temporary SML builtins for printing strings and terminating with an integer exit code, so the compiler has a runnable baseline before the Basis Library exists.
close_reason: Implemented temporary print and exit builtins with lexer/parser/codegen modules and span-based diagnostics.

title: Add Clap backend debugging options
description: Replace manual CLI parsing with clap and expose backend diagnostics: IR dumps, verification, optimization level, timings, stats, textual assembly, and object disassembly.
close_reason: Replaced manual parsing with clap and added IR dumps, verification, optimization levels, timings, stats, assembly output, and objdump mode.

title: Add target assembly output mode
description: Add --asm to emit Cranelift's target-specific lowered instruction listing to a .S file instead of linking an executable.
acceptance_criteria: --asm writes a .S file and does not invoke the linker; normal binary compilation and --debug-passes remain functional; documentation explains the emitted listing.
close_reason: Added --asm mode, documented its disassembly semantics, and verified binary/debug modes remain functional.

title: Add Cranelift debug pass output flag
description: Add a CLI flag that exposes Cranelift IR and post-lowering instruction output for debugging without changing normal compilation.
acceptance_criteria: Normal compilation remains unchanged; --debug-passes emits useful compiler-stage output; tests cover flag behavior or the exposed output path.
close_reason: Added --debug-passes with pre/post-optimization IR and lowered machine instruction output, documented and tested.

title: Implement required Basis collections and I/O
description: Implement required Vector, Array, slice, text I/O, stream I/O, and BinIO interfaces in dependency order. Cover boundary cases, exceptions, and resource handling with fixtures.

title: Implement required Basis OS and process interfaces
description: Implement required OS, OS.FileSys, OS.Path, OS.Process, CommandLine, and time/date interfaces, preserving platform-sensitive behavior and marking optional portions.

title: Audit optional Basis components and portability
description: Compare Nassau’s Basis coverage with the specification’s optional components, record compatibility differences against SML/NJ and MLton, and add fixtures for portable common behavior.

title: Implement required primitive Basis types and datatypes
description: Implement the required top-level environment and primitive Basis types and datatypes, including Bool, List, Option, Order, Unit, Int/Word/Real families as supported by the chosen target model. Follow specified types, equality properties, and overflow/exception behavior.

title: Implement required Basis arithmetic and string structures
description: Implement required Int, Word, Real, Math, String, Substring, Char, and related primitive structures. Separate specified semantics from implementation-dependent numeric edge cases and test portable behavior.

title: Implement the Standard ML Basis Library
description: After the SML’97 language core is substantially implemented and the conformance inventory is established, implement the required Standard ML Basis Library interfaces and behavior. Treat the official Basis specification as authoritative and keep optional facilities explicitly scoped.
acceptance_criteria: Required Basis components are implemented and covered with fixture-based tests, with optional components and platform-specific behavior tracked separately.
